NNI should remain in the underfollowed lane as a second-order campus payments, tuition management, loan servicing systems, and education technology infrastructure provider hidden inside a financial-services conglomerate.

COUR is a platform-layer candidate for online university degrees, micro-credentials, and campus learning infrastructure, but it requires careful separation from generic consumer online-course exposure.
Healthcare-oriented online/hybrid programs introduce a scarce regulated-input layer: clinical placements, simulation capacity, accreditation, hospital affiliations, and program approval timelines.

Search did not yet identify many pure-play public vendors supplying simulation equipment, proctoring, enrollment marketing, compliance, or clinical-placement software specifically to university OPM programs; these may be private-company dominated or embedded inside larger software/services firms.

node: University services and online program management
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the university services and OPM node found a small set of US-listed companies tied to the hard-to-replace operating layer behind online, hybrid, workforce, and healthcare education programs. The strongest chokepoint angles are not generic online-course delivery, but institutional trust, regulated enrollment/payment infrastructure, university partner relationships, healthcare program capacity, clinical/simulation infrastructure, and long-duration operating systems that become costly for schools to replace. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
